name: Pedal Mod for Grand Piano part 1 of 2 - Push Rod Brackets.

captions.detailed: This 3D-printable model consists of two separate components: a two-part frame clamp and a long, adjustable support arm. The clamp has a rectangular central opening with side mounting tabs, a vertical cylinder hinge on one corner, and small bolt holes for securing around a frame. The support arm features two long parallel rails with a series of multiple positioning holes, a central solid block, and larger circular openings at the opposite fork-like end to hold a push-rod.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric piano knee-pedal modification kit in OpenSCAD containing a two-part frame clamp and an adjustable support arm. The script should use adjustable parameters for PedFrameDepth, PedFrameWidth, and PushRodDiameter to customize the clamp size and the rod guide holes.
captions.factory: The code uses two distinct difference() blocks. The first block builds the frame clamp by unioning cubes and a cylinder (for the hinge strength) and then subtracting a central cube for the frame slot, a thin horizontal cube to split the clamp into two halves, and cylindrical screw holes. The second block constructs the support arm by starting with a long rectangular block, subtracting a perpendicular cylinder for the push-rod guide, subtracting large rectangular sections to form the parallel fork structures, and subtracting a series of translated cylinders to create the row of adjustment holes.
